title: Naming Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Common and IUPAC Names
subject: Chemistry
objective: Every halide has two correct names. The common name is the alkyl group + halide (isopropyl chloride, ethyl chloride). The IUPAC name writes the halogen as a prefix (fluoro, chloro, bromo, iodo) on the longest chain, numbered from the end that gives the lowest locants; when both ends tie, alphabetical order decides (2-bromo-3-methylbutane). On benzene one halogen keeps the same name (chlorobenzene); two use o-, m-, p- in common names and 1,2 / 1,3 / 1,4 in IUPAC.

fill.q: In common names, the alkyl group name is followed by the name of the ____.

p- in a dihalobenzene corresponds to the IUPAC numbers ____.

tf.q: Ethyl bromide is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂Br.
tf.explain: It is the common name; IUPAC: bromoethane.
Cl is on the middle carbon, 2 from either end.

tf.q: Alphabetical order decides numbering before the lowest-locant rule.

tf.explain: One carbon between the two Cl.

ar.a: Assertion: BrCH₂CH₂Cl is 1-bromo-2-chloroethane. Reason: When locants tie, the prefix first in alphabetical order gets the lower number.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

ar.a: Assertion: Chlorobenzene has different common and IUPAC names. Reason: Haloarenes are named with o-, m-, p- in the common system.

mcq.explain: Br on a carbon with three CH₃.
